gloss: to push into, to break into, to force one's way in

definitions.explanation: To forcefully push something or someone into a space.

definitions.gloss: to break into, to force one's way in
definitions.explanation: To enter a place by force, especially illegally.

examples.japanese: かばんに{本|ほん}を{押|お}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I shoved the book into my bag.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}を{無理|むり}やり{押|お}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I forcibly pushed the luggage in.

examples.japanese: {服|ふく}を{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しに{押|お}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I shoved the clothes into the drawer.

examples.japanese: {満員|まんいん}の{電車|でんしゃ}に{体|からだ}を{押|お}し{入|い}れて、なんとか{乗|の}った。
examples.english: I squeezed my body into the packed train and managed to get on.

examples.japanese: スーツケースに{土産|みやげ}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{押|お}し{入|い}れるのは{大変|たいへん}だった。
examples.english: It was hard to shove all the souvenirs into the suitcase.

examples.japanese: {強盗|ごうとう}が{家|いえ}に{押|お}し{入|い}れた。
{群衆|ぐんしゅう}が{建物|たてもの}に{押|お}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: The crowd forced their way into the building.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}が{窓|まど}から{押|お}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: The thief broke in through the window.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}は{裏口|うらぐち}から{店|みせ}に{押|お}し{入|い}れたらしい。
examples.english: The culprit apparently broke into the store through the back door.

examples.japanese: {深夜|しんや}に{見知|みし}らぬ{男|おとこ}が{家|いえ}に{押|お}し{入|い}れてきて、{警察|けいさつ}を{呼|よ}んだ。
examples.english: A stranger forced his way into the house late at night, and we called the police.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB:
Formed from {押|お}す (to push) + {入|い}れる (to put in). Indicates forceful entry or insertion.

TRANSITIVITY:
{他動詞|たどうし} (transitive verb) for sense 1
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive verb) for sense 2 (person as subject)

NOTE:
Do not confuse with {押|お}し{入|い}れ (おしいれ), which means "closet" (noun).
